findings.reason: UNTRUSTED SOURCE: store_admin_alias_guid() is the .store callback for per-port admin-alias-GUID sysfs attributes (lines 68-70, wired via create_sysfs_entry at line 164/180); its buf is arbitrary-format user bytes. MISSING GUARANTEE: the stack local sysadmin_ag_val (declared line 78, never initialized) is the out-param of sscanf(buf, '%llx', &sysadmin_ag_val) at line 88, and the sscanf return code (number of conversions; 0/EOF on non-numeric input, e.g. an empty or 'nope' write) is completely ignored — exactly the seed's invariant that a parse out-param is only defined on success. UNSAFE USE: on parse failure sysadmin_ag_val still holds uninitialized stack bytes and is consumed twice — stored into mdev->sriov.alias_guid.ports_guid[].all_rec_per_port[record_num].all_recs[GUID_REC_SIZE*guid_index_in_rec] (lines 89-92) and committed via mlx4_set_admin_guid(mdev->dev, cpu_to_be64(sysadmin_ag_val), ...) (lines 97-99), plus state transition to MLX4_GUID_INFO_STATUS_IDLE (95-96) and alias-guid work scheduling (106), so garbage becomes persistent device/GUID-table state that is later re-read and re-applied to the InfiniBand SM. COUNTEREVIDENCE CHECKED: I verified show_admin_alias_guid reads back only the stored value, that no earlier memset/initializer touches sysadmin_ag_val in this function, and that all other sscanf callers in the tree either check the conversion count or pre-initialize; impact is bounded because the sysfs node is root-writable (DEVICE_ATTR admin mode) so this is a garbage-state/uninitialized-value variant rather than an unprivileged stack disclosure — hence medium, not high, confidence.

UNTRUSTED SOURCE: iscsi_if_set_param() handles ISCSI_UEVENT_SET_PARAM netlink messages (dispatched at line 3974); the payload string data is fully attacker-controlled (gated only by netlink_capable(skb, CAP_SYS_ADMIN) at line 3894, so privileged). MISSING GUARANTEE: sscanf(data, '%d', &value) at line 3015 ignores its return, so a non-numeric payload performs zero conversions. UNSAFE USE: session->recovery_tmo = value at line 3017 still executes — value is pre-initialized to 0 at line 2998, so this is not a stack leak, but the failed parse silently coerces the session recovery timeout to 0 (immediate-failover semantics) instead of rejecting the write, and the write-side commit is not gated on the parse. COUNTEREVIDENCE CHECKED: value initialization removes the uninitialized-disclosure reading; CAP_SYS_ADMIN requirement limits exposure; the default branch correctly propagates transport->set_param errors. Kept as a low-confidence adjacent variant of the seed's unchecked-parse-outparam mechanism (unchecked parse -> unconditional state commit).

candidates.reason: nla_parse_nested() return ignored in nl80211_process_links, but __nla_validate_parse() in lib/nlattr.c memsets the tb out-array before parsing, and attrs here is kzalloc'd and re-memset each iteration, so failure leaves NULL pointers which are NULL-checked.
tb[NL80211_PMSR_PEER_ATTR_MAX+1] and req[] are zeroed by the parser before returning; presence checks guard every nla_data use.
memcpy(&bt, nla_data(...), sizeof(bt)) copies from a policy-validated NLA_BINARY attribute of exact struct size; all subsequent validation errors return.
daddr copied from length-validated attr and immediately value-checked.
gid copied from attr enforced by strict min-length NLA policy; handler is a kernel-to-kernel RDMA netlink LS response, not direct userspace.
sscanf result ignored but dev_id pre-initialized to -1 and range-checked; opt_buf pre-NUL-terminated; bad input rejected.

sscanf result ignored and value potentially uninitialized on parse failure, but value is only tested for non-zero to produce an -EPROTO; worst case is a spurious error return, no state commit or disclosure.
kstrtou32 return checked (if (val) return) and sscanf conversion counts compared to expected values.

sscanf(...)==0 checked so all-zero-conversion fails closed; rate would be uninitialized only if sscanf returned 1 while %i failed, which glibc/kernel sscanf does not do; partial pre-initialized to false; root-only debugfs; not fully audited for callers.
sscanf conversion count checked (cnt == 2 / cnt == 1) before register access.

unchecked copy_from_sockptr(&max_optlen) is a documented best-effort read of the user length for the legacy !compat getsockopt path; koptlen is separately validated inside sockptr_to_sockopt; no state commit from the unchecked copy.

limitations: Scope was bounded to high-signal patterns (ignored nla_parse/nla_memcpy return codes, unchecked sscanf/kstrto*/copy_from_sockptr/copy_struct_from_user in non-sysctl write surfaces); a fully automated per-function dataflow pass was not run, so an unchecked parse in a less idiomatic pattern could be missed.

The mlx4 finding's exploitability as a stack disclosure is bounded: the attribute is admin-writable (root) and show_admin_alias_guid reads back the stored value, so I report it as an uninitialized-stack-value-to-persistent-state variant, not an unprivileged information leak; on-stack attacker influence over sysadmin_ag_val was not measured.
The iscsi finding was not traced into all iSCSI transports' recovery_tmo consumers, so the operational impact of a silently-zeroed recovery timeout is asserted from the field semantics only.

The iwlwifi mld candidate remains unresolved (strong evidence of safety but caller-side analysis incomplete); drivers/tty/serial serial_core and a handful of fbdev/omapfb sysfs stores named in the heuristic list were not individually deep-read.
